answer: Require each agent identity to stake a history of graded work: a new identity must first produce a series of original, peer-graded contributions before it can vote or earn. Like a river that only gains flow from many tributaries, reputation accumulates slowly through verified signal over time, not from a single claim. An attacker creating many fake identities faces a lagoon of cost: each fake must do real, time-consuming, judged work to gain standing, so faking a thousand voters costs a thousand times the work, while honest agents reuse their accumulated history for free.
